findings.F1: The tested shortfall is on the side the idea predicts but too small to show at 5 days: the mean is +0.32 % per case (t 0.74, 559 cases, strength 0.033). On the same cases it is +0.53 % over 24 hours (t 2.51, 572 cases), +0.60 % over 72 hours (t 1.60), and nearly gone at 240 hours (+0.06 %, t 0.08). The fade happens in the first day, and the plan's 5-day horizon dilutes it with four days of noise.
findings.F2: Over 24 hours the shortfall is graded the way the idea says. Among surges after a 7-day fall (458 events), the deeper the vol-scaled fall, the lower the next 24-hour return (corr 0.17, t 3.74), and the larger the surge, the lower that return (corr 0.15, t 3.31). In the deepest third of falls the 24-hour shortfall is 1.35 % (t 3.45); in the other two thirds it is about zero (-0.31 % and -0.08 %).
findings.F3: At 5 days the effect is mixed across coins and years, which is why the t stays low. The shortfall is +1.84 % on ETH (t 2.15) and +1.13 % on XRP, but -1.40 % on ZEC. By year it runs from +1.57 % in 2025 (t 1.65) to -2.66 % in 2024 (t -2.42, the price rose more than usual).
findings.F4: Surges that follow a 7-day rise behave the other way: they continue by +2.2 % above drift over 120 hours (t 2.74, 328 events) and +4.4 % over 240 hours (t 3.47). This gain is not graded by the surge's size (smallest third +3.9 %, largest +1.4 % at 120 hours). It is concentrated in XRP (+8.6 %) and in 2020 and 2024, so it does not support an idea of its own.
findings.F5: On size, the 5-day test's total move is -0.33 % per case against a 0.19 % round trip, because the coins' normal rise works against a short. The 24-hour shortfall of 0.53 % is about 2.8 times that cost, and the deepest third's 1.35 % is about 7 times it.

ideas.name: post-selloff surge fades, more coins
ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside after its 7-day return before that day was a fall, the price rises less than the coin's usual 5-day return over the next 5 days; the deeper that 7-day fall, the larger the shortfall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a sharp up day after a week of heavy selling as a relief bounce to fade or ignore, not a breakout to hold for days.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside after its 7-day return before that day was a fall, the price rises less than the coin's usual 1-day return over the next 24 hours; the deeper that 7-day fall, the larger the shortfall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a sharp up day after a week of heavy selling for one day only, most strongly after the deepest falls, rather than hold the fade for a week.
ideas.name: post-selloff surge fades within a day
